profile.reading: This listing is named for its own street address, 505 Marquette Avenue NW, a building in downtown Albuquerque's office core, rather than for any data center operator or brand. Naming a facility after its own address, instead of an operator or campus name, is a pattern typical of general purpose office towers, not of purpose built data centers, which are almost always branded distinctly by the company that operates them. No leasing site, property listing, or operator page could be independently confirmed to establish what currently occupies 505 Marquette Avenue NW or whether it hosts any telecommunications equipment room or meet me room serving downtown Albuquerque tenants. Downtown office towers of this era commonly include a shared telecom closet or fiber entry point used to bring connectivity into the building, the kind of infrastructure that sometimes gets tagged as a data center on mapping platforms even though the building functions as ordinary leased office space. Without a confirmed operator, published capacity, or any business record specific to a data center use at this address, this entry is recorded as an unconfirmed downtown office building rather than a verified data center.

reading.body:
505 Marquette is an unconfirmed data center entry, and New Mexico's mapped data center count has no published capacity behind it.

The building is named for its own street address rather than an operator or campus brand. That naming pattern fits a general purpose office tower, not a purpose built data center, which is almost always branded by the company that runs it. Downtown office towers of this era commonly hold a shared telecom closet or fiber entry point, and that kind of infrastructure sometimes gets tagged as a data center on mapping platforms. No operator, capacity figure, or business record specific to a data center use at this address could be confirmed.

The state context matters more than the building. New Mexico has 14 facilities tagged as data centers on OpenStreetMap and zero with published power capacity from operator specification pages. This entry ranks first in the state by published megawatts only because every other mapped facility also publishes nothing. That ranking measures the absence of data, not infrastructure.

For AI scaling and grid constraint analysis, this entry carries no usable signal. It has no confirmed specifications, no operator identity, and no independent verification of data center operations. What the data does not cover is equally plain: it cannot say whether a meet me room or telecom closet exists here, who occupies the building, or how much power any New Mexico facility draws. The one hard geographic fact is that it sits 4.2 miles from Albuquerque International Sunport.
